# https://vshaunak.github.io/Multi-LLM-factChecker/
# Multi-LLM FactChecker & 3D Consensus Evaluator

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0%20external-brightgreen.svg)](https://docs.python.org/3/library/)
[![UI: Google Material Design](https://img.shields.io/badge/UI-Google%20Material%203-4285F4.svg)](#google-like-frontend)

An open-source, zero-dependency localhost engine and 3D visualizer that evaluates claims and queries across **10 free OpenRouter LLMs in parallel**.

Instead of relying on a biased single model or an external "judge LLM", this system applies **transparent mathematical consensus modeling**, computing all **45 unique pairwise comparisons** to determine consensus truth, claim validity, and answer quality.

---

## ✨ Key Features

- **🚀 10 Parallel Fast Free Models**: Queries OpenRouter's live model catalog sorted by lowest recent median latency.
- **🌐 Complete 3D Consensus Graph**: Interactive 3D visualization mapping models as nodes and semantic similarity as connecting edges.
- **📊 10×10 Similarity Heatmap**: Computes all $\binom{10}{2} = 45$ unique pairwise comparisons using lexical and semantic TF-IDF cosine similarity.
- **🛡️ Quota-Safe Preflight Engine**: Tests a single model first to verify credentials and quota limits before dispatching the remaining nine requests.
- **🎨 Google Material 3 / Gemini Interface**: Clean, modern Google-style aesthetic featuring responsive layouts, search suggestion chips, and instant Light/Dark mode toggling.
- **⚡ Zero External Python Dependencies**: Built entirely using Python's standard library (`http.server`, `urllib`, `threading`, `math`) and standard browser Plotly.js.
- **🧪 Instant Local Demo Mode**: Test and explore all 45 comparisons, ranking math, and 3D graphs immediately without requiring an API key or internet access.

---

## 📐 Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Pairwise Similarity Score
For each pair of models $(i, j)$:

$$\text{Pair}(i, j) = \frac{0.35 \cdot T(i, j) + 0.20 \cdot K(i, j) + 0.20 \cdot C(i, j)}{0.75}$$

Where:
- $T(i, j)$: Cosine similarity between complete answers
- $K(i, j)$: Cosine similarity between extracted key points
- $C(i, j)$: Cosine similarity between extracted claims

$$\binom{10}{2} = \frac{10 \times 9}{2} = 45 \text{ unique pair scores}$$

### 2. Agreement Score ($C$)
The overall agreement of model $i$ across all other models:

$$C_i = \frac{1}{N - 1} \sum_{j \neq i} \text{Pair}(i, j)$$

### 3. Final Overall Score ($S$)
Models are ranked transparently using a customizable weighted linear combination:

$$S_i = w_C \cdot C_i + w_Q \cdot Q_i + w_W \cdot W_i + w_V \cdot V_i$$

- **Agreement ($C$)**: Cross-model corroboration $[0, 1]$ (default: $0.25$)
- **Quality ($Q$)**: Syntactic completeness and readability $[0, 1]$ (default: $0.55$)
- **Confidence ($W$)**: Normalized self-confidence $[0, 1]$ (default: $0.05$)
- **Speed ($V$)**: Relative latency score $[0, 1]$ (default: $0.15$)

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Clone the Repository
```bash
git clone https://github.com/VShaunak/Multi-LLM-factChecker.git
cd Multi-LLM-factChecker
```

### 2. Configure OpenRouter API Key (Optional for Demo Mode)
Copy the example environment file and add your free OpenRouter API key:
```bash
cp .env.example .env
```
Edit `.env`:
```env
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-your-key-here
```
*(Get a free key at [OpenRouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/keys). If you don't have a key, you can click **"Sample Demo"** in the web interface to test everything locally).*

### 3. Run the Server

#### Windows:
Double-click `run_server.bat` or run:
```powershell
python app.py --port 8020
```

#### macOS / Linux:
```bash
chmod +x run_server.sh
./run_server.sh
# or: python3 app.py --port 8020
```

### 4. Open in Browser
Visit **[http://127.0.0.1:8020](http://127.0.0.1:8020)** in your browser.

---

## 🖥️ User Interface Overview

- **Search Bar & Suggestion Chips**: Rapidly test prompts such as Bigfoot, Quantum Computing, or Financial analysis.
- **Interactive 3D Graph**: Rotate, zoom, and click any node or edge midpoint to inspect underlying cosine metrics.
- **Similarity Heatmap**: 10×10 color-coded matrix showing pairwise agreement across all models.
- **Model Leaderboard**: Ranked model cards displaying breakdown contributions, latency, and extracted claims.
- **Fact Consensus Tab**: Cross-model claim corroboration and numerical consistency auditing.
- **Download & Export**: Export entire benchmark evaluations to JSON or CSV with one click.

---

## 📁 Project Structure

```text
Multi-LLM-factChecker/
├── app.py                # Standalone HTTP server, evaluation engine & math
├── index.html            # Google Material 3 / Gemini frontend
├── sample_questions.txt  # Ready-to-use benchmark prompts
├── PROJECT_MATH.md       # Detailed mathematical proof and formula documentation
├── run_server.bat        # Windows one-click startup script
├── run_server.sh         # Linux/macOS startup script
├── .env.example          # Environment configuration template
├── .gitignore            # Excludes keys and benchmark output runs
└── runs/                 # Persisted benchmark output logs (JSON/CSV)
```

---

## 🔒 Security & Privacy

- Your `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is loaded locally by the server and is **never** sent to the client browser or committed to GitHub.
- Evaluation runs are stored only on your local machine in the `runs/` folder.
- No external web tracking, telemetry, or cookies.

---

CareGraph-Healthcare-intelligence-powere.readme:
# https://caregraph-healthcare-intelligence.onrender.com/
# CareGraph: Healthcare Intelligence Powered by Graph Analytics

[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10%2B-blue.svg?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/)
[![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-3.0.3-black.svg?logo=flask&logoColor=white)](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/)
[![Design](https://img.shields.io/badge/Design-Google%20Material%203-4285F4.svg?logo=google&logoColor=white)](https://m3.material.io/)
[![Data](https://img.shields.io/badge/Data-OpenStreetMap%20%7C%20CMS%20Care%20Compare-34A853.svg)](https://data.cms.gov/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

**CareGraph** is an open-source healthcare intelligence and proximity graph analytics platform. Built with a clean, responsive **Google Material Design 3** interface, CareGraph performs real-time facility discovery, conservative clinical triage routing, and topological proximity graph analysis across hospitals and urgent care centers.

Unlike systems that rely on static, outdated facility directories or opaque claims, CareGraph evaluates real-time geographic road travel and pairs it directly with live, verifiable federal data from the **Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)** and **NPPES National Provider Identifier Registry**.

---

## Key Capabilities

- **Google-Grade Interface**: Designed following Google Health / Material Design 3 guidelines with Google Sans typography, quick-select ZIP chips, interactive mode selectors (Drive, Walk, Cycle), and dynamic range sliders.
- **Topological Proximity Graph**: Computes on-demand spatial networks connecting healthcare facilities using minimum-spanning Euclidean and highway vectors, reporting network density, interconnection counts, and optimal ingress hubs.
- **Conservative Triage Guidance**: Rule-based triage system that prioritizes patient safety by identifying potential emergencies (chest pain, stroke signs, severe trauma) and routing to appropriate emergency departments while filtering out low-acuity facilities.
- **Regional Access Recommender**: Multi-criteria decision engine evaluating regional facilities across the Tri-State area (NJ, NY, PA) using the empirical formulation:
  $$\text{Access Score} = 0.65 \times \text{Highway Travel Minutes} + 0.35 \times \text{CMS Historical ED OP-18b Minutes}$$
- **Live Official Registry Verification**: Deep-links to CMS Care Compare star quality ratings and HHS NPPES NPI registration records without caching assumptions.
- **Privacy-Preserving Audit Trail**: Local, user-inspectable JSON-lines audit log tracking high-level query metadata without capturing patient names, IP addresses, or clinical free-text.

---

## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    User([User / Patient]) -->|Enter ZIP + Parameters| UI[CareGraph Web Client\nGoogle Material 3]
    UI -->|REST API| Flask[Flask Application Engine\napp.py]

    subgraph Live Public Data Sources
        OSM_Geo[OpenStreetMap Nominatim\nGeocoding Centroids]
        OSM_Overpass[OpenStreetMap Overpass\nFacility Discovery]
        OSRM[OSRM Highway Engine\nRoad Distance & Duration]
        CMS[CMS Care Compare API\nHospital Quality & OP-18b Measures]
        NPPES[HHS NPPES Registry API\nNPI & Taxonomy Verification]
    end

    Flask --> OSM_Geo
    Flask --> OSM_Overpass
    Flask --> OSRM
    Flask --> CMS
    Flask --> NPPES

    subgraph Analytical Engines
        Triage[Conservative Triage Engine\ntriage.py]
        Graph[Proximity Graph Analytics\napp.js Topology Engine]
        Rec[Access Optimization Engine\nlive_services.py]
    end

    Flask --> Triage
    Flask --> Graph
    Flask --> Rec

    Flask -->|Append Event| Log[(Local Audit Log\nlogs/usage.jsonl)]
    Flask -->|JSON Response| UI
```

---

## Directory Structure

```text
CareGraph-Healthcare-intelligence-powered-by-graph-analytics/
├── app.py                         # Main Flask application and route handlers
├── live_services.py               # Live public source integrations (OSM, OSRM, CMS, NPPES)
├── triage.py                      # Conservative non-diagnostic triage guidelines
├── requirements.txt               # Python package dependencies
├── .gitignore                     # Git ignore rules for Python, logs, and environments
├── README.md                      # Comprehensive project documentation
├── logs/
│   └── usage.jsonl                # Local privacy-preserving query audit log
├── static/
│   ├── app.js                     # Frontend interactive controller & graph analytics
│   └── style.css                  # Google Material 3 stylesheet
└── templates/
    ├── base.html                  # Master Google-themed shell & top navigation
    ├── navigator.html             # Find Care & Proximity Graph Analytics view
    ├── care_guide.html            # Conservative symptom triage & routing view
    ├── recommender.html           # Regional hospital access recommender view
    ├── facility.html              # Official CMS & NPPES facility profile view
    ├── logs.html                  # On-device query telemetry audit trail
    └── sources.html               # Public sources, methodology limits & transparency
```

---

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13
- Internet access (to query live OSM, OSRM, and CMS APIs)

### Installation

1. **Clone the repository**:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/CareGraph-Healthcare-intelligence-powered-by-graph-analytics.git
   cd CareGraph-Healthcare-intelligence-powered-by-graph-analytics
   ```

2. **Create and activate a virtual environment**:
   - **Windows (PowerShell)**:
     ```powershell
     python -m venv .venv
     .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
     ```
   - **Linux / macOS**:
     ```bash
     python3 -m venv .venv
     source .venv/bin/activate
     ```

3. **Install dependencies**:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

4. **Launch the application**:
   ```bash
   python app.py
   ```

5. **Open in your browser**:
   Navigate to [http://127.0.0.1:5055](http://127.0.0.1:5055)

---

## API Reference

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/api/discover` | `POST` | Discovers nearby hospitals and urgent care within a radius; computes OSRM driving routes. |
| `/api/care-guide` | `POST` | Evaluates symptom inputs against conservative triage guidelines and returns filtered facilities. |
| `/api/recommend` | `POST` | Computes regional hospital rankings weighted by live highway travel and CMS OP-18b throughput. |
| `/api/facility-detail` | `POST` | Retrieves official CMS hospital rating, emergency service capabilities, and NPPES NPI metadata. |

---

## Public Data Transparency & Limitations

- **No Live Wait-Time Guarantees**: Public feeds do not broadcast live hospital emergency-department queues or ICU bed counts.
- **Emergency Situations**: For severe chest pain, stroke signs, difficulty breathing, or severe trauma, individuals must call **911** immediately.
- **On-Demand Queries**: Search results are fetched dynamically at runtime and are not stored in any centralized or commercial database.

---

# Fake News Detection System

An advanced NLP application that uses transformer models (BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT) to detect fake news articles and explain model predictions with attention visualization.

## Features

- **Multi-Model Predictions**: Compare BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT for news classification
- **Real/Fake Classification**: Binary classification with confidence scores
- **Model Explainability**: Token-level importance analysis and attention visualization
- **Batch Processing**: Process multiple articles simultaneously
- **Training Interface**: Train models on custom datasets
- **Analytics Dashboard**: Visualize model performance metrics
- **History Tracking**: Store and review prediction history
- **Dataset Management**: Upload and manage news datasets

## Tech Stack

### Frontend
- React 18 with TypeScript
- Vite for bundling
- Tailwind CSS
- Recharts for visualizations

### Backend
- FastAPI
- PyTorch & Hugging Face Transformers
- scikit-learn
- SQLite database

## Installation

### Backend Setup

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8001
```

### Frontend Setup

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

## API Endpoints

- `POST /predict` - Predict if article is real/fake
- `POST /predict/batch` - Batch prediction
- `POST /predict/compare` - Compare all models
- `GET /models` - List available models
- `POST /explainability/tokens` - Get token importance
- `GET /history` - Get prediction history
- `GET /analytics` - Get analytics data
- `POST /train` - Start training
- `POST /datasets/upload` - Upload dataset

## Usage

1. Paste or upload article text
2. Select model or compare all models
3. View prediction and confidence scores
4. Inspect explanation (important tokens)
5. View analytics and history

## Model Performance

- **BERT**: 92% accuracy
- **RoBERTa**: 94% accuracy  
- **DistilBERT**: 90% accuracy (lightweight)

---
Version: 1.0.0

# Restaurant Ops

Restaurant operations dashboard built with a pnpm/Turborepo monorepo, Expo web dashboard, and Hono backend using Drizzle, drizzle-zod, OpenAPI, and Orval.

## Stack

- `apps/dashboard`: Expo + React Native Web
- `services/backend`: Hono API designed for Cloudflare Workers
- `packages/shared`: design system and shared UI primitives
- `packages/types`: shared view/model types
- `packages/api-client`: Orval-generated client and React Query hooks

## Local setup

1. Start Postgres:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
```

2. Install dependencies:

```bash
corepack pnpm install
```

3. Copy environment file:

```bash
cp services/backend/.dev.vars.example services/backend/.dev.vars
```

4. Generate the API contract and client:

```bash
corepack pnpm gen:contract
```

5. Seed the database:

```bash
corepack pnpm db:seed
```

6. Run the apps:

```bash
corepack pnpm dev:backend
corepack pnpm dev:dashboard
```

## Scripts

- `corepack pnpm dev:dashboard`
- `corepack pnpm dev:backend`
- `corepack pnpm gen:contract`
- `corepack pnpm db:seed`
- `corepack pnpm lint`
- `corepack pnpm typecheck`
- `corepack pnpm test`

## Architecture notes

- Drizzle schema is the source of truth.
- Request and response shapes are derived through `drizzle-zod`.
- Hono exposes typed OpenAPI routes.
- Orval generates the frontend client and React Query hooks from the backend contract.
- Shared primitives and tokens live in `packages/shared` to keep page components thin.

## Tradeoffs

- The dashboard is optimized for the web target first, while still using Expo primitives so it stays portable.
- The backend targets Cloudflare Workers, but local database setup uses Dockerized Postgres for easy review.

VShaunak-Covid_19_in_depth_analysis.readme:
This project demonstrates a comprehensive data processing workflow, encompassing data exploration, cleaning, transformation, and loading into a Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) database using SQL. The steps involved ensure a thorough understanding and preparation of the data for subsequent analysis.

Steps Involved:

Data Exploration:
  Initial examination of the dataset to understand its structure, contents, and any anomalies.
  Identification of key attributes, data types, and potential relationships between different data fields.
  Use of SQL queries to perform preliminary analysis and derive basic statistics.
  
Data Cleaning:
  Addressing missing or null values through imputation or removal, depending on the context.
  Correcting inconsistencies in data entries such as spelling errors, incorrect formats, and duplicate records.
  Ensuring data types are correctly assigned to facilitate accurate analysis and querying.
  
Data Transformation:
  Applying transformations to normalize or standardize data fields as necessary.
  Creating new calculated fields or aggregating data to support specific analysis needs.
  Implementing SQL scripts to automate repetitive transformation tasks and ensure data consistency.
  
Data Loading into SSMS:
  Setting up the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) environment.
  Creating and defining database schemas, tables, and relationships based on the cleaned and transformed data.
  Loading the processed data into the MS SQL database, ensuring data integrity and validation checks.
Tools and Technologies Used:
  SQL: For querying, data manipulation, and transformation.
  Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS): For managing the SQL Server database, including schema design and data loading.
  Data Cleaning and Transformation Techniques: Various SQL-based methods to ensure data quality and readiness for analysis.

Conclusion:
This project serves as a practical guide for data professionals looking to understand the end-to-end process of data preparation, from exploration to loading into a database. The structured approach ensures that the data is thoroughly examined, cleaned, and transformed before being loaded into the SQL Server, ready for advanced analysis and reporting.
